application_method: Apply for admission to the chosen Kozminski University undergraduate programme through the Kozminski University Admissions Portal (kozminski.my.site.com/AdmissionsPortal)

Candidates whose documents were issued outside the EU, EFTA, OECD, Ukraine or China must pass the online 20-minute closed-ended knowledge test (at least 30% correct answers) before entering the admission process

new_scholarship.description: Kozminski University awards a Scholarship for the Best Students covering 100% of tuition fees to students admitted to the first semester of full-time or part-time undergraduate (Bachelor's) or long-cycle Master's programmes. Eligibility requires at least 600 admission points from three different, freely chosen subjects in the written section of the final examinations, together with the highest total on a ranking list created separately for each programme and study format. For the 2026/2027 cycle the university published 17 full-time scholarships (7 for Polish-language undergraduate programmes, 7 for English-language undergraduate programmes and 3 for the long-cycle Master's in Law) and 3 part-time scholarships (1 for Polish-language undergraduate programmes and 2 for the long-cycle Master's in Law). The scholarship is initially awarded for the first semester and can be extended to the second subject to a minimum GPA of 4.60 on a 5.0 scale; the Olympiad winner and Olympiad finalist scholarships carry the same GPA condition for continuation. The award covers tuition fees only and includes no stipend, travel allowance or accommodation support.
new_scholarship.best_fit: A secondary-school graduate with very high final-examination results (at least 600 admission points) who can realistically top the ranking list for one specific Kozminski University undergraduate programme and study format, who can self-fund living costs, accommodation and travel, and who can sustain a GPA of at least 4.60 on a 5.0 scale in order to extend the award into the second semester.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to students admitted to the first semester of a full-time or part-time undergraduate (Bachelor's) or long-cycle Master's programme at Kozminski University; no nationality or residency restriction is published. Selection requires at least 600 admission points from three different, freely chosen subjects in the written section of the final examinations, and the highest total on a ranking list created separately for each programme and study format. Admission points convert at 1.5 points per 1% at basic level, 2 points per 1% at extended level except mathematics, 2.5 points per 1% at bilingual level and 3 points per 1% in extended mathematics. Continuation into the second semester requires a minimum GPA of 4.60 on a 5.0 scale. The regulations do not apply to the Bachelor in Management - Sustainable Business programme, which has a separate Sustainability Leaders Scholarship, and the scholarship is not automatic on admission: a separate application is required after the student is admitted.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: The Scholarship Committee awards the scholarship on the student's application after admission. Ranking lists are created separately for each programme and study format, so competition is within the applicant's own programme rather than university-wide, and 7 of the 17 full-time scholarships are reserved for English-language undergraduate programmes. Admission points convert at 1.5 points per 1% at basic level, 2 points per 1% at extended level except mathematics, 2.5 points per 1% at bilingual level and 3 points per 1% in extended mathematics. There is no interview or portfolio stage published. A separate Rector's scholarship is available to first-year students admitted to undergraduate or long-cycle Master's programmes on the basis of Olympiad laureate/finalist status or a medal from at least the Polish Championship sports competition, or alternatively on outstanding academic results (high GPA from the previous academic year) or scientific/artistic achievements.

The university states that in 2024 it funded scholarships for 49 people for a total of over PLN 160,000; that is a funding-scale data point, not an award value. Cycle figures (award counts, tuition, point thresholds) are re-published by the university for each academic year and may differ for 2027/2028.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the current admission registration window on the specific programme page, because the scholarship itself has no separate deadline and hinges on admission

Compute your admission points with the published conversion table (1.5 points per 1% basic, 2 points per 1% extended except mathematics, 2.5 points per 1% bilingual, 3 points per 1% extended mathematics) and check you clear the 600-point threshold
Identify which programme and study format you are competing in, because ranking lists are drawn separately and the scholarship pool for English-language undergraduate programmes is only 7 places
Register on the Kozminski University Admissions Portal and pay the PLN 85 admission fee early rather than at the deadline

If your school documents were issued outside the EU, EFTA, OECD, Ukraine or China, prepare for the 20-minute online knowledge test on high-school social sciences and arrange the NAWA statement or recognition decision, since both are needed before admission
Plan for living costs, accommodation and travel separately: the award pays tuition only
Watch for the scholarship application form by email after admission, and submit it promptly, since the award is not automatic
Plan your first year to protect a GPA of at least 4.60 on a 5.0 scale, without which the award cannot be extended into the second semester
If you are applying to the Sustainable Business major, check its separate Sustainability Leaders Scholarship instead, because the general rules exclude it
common_rejection_risks: Falling below the 600 admission-point threshold or not topping the programme ranking list: the pool is only 7 full-time scholarships for all English-language undergraduate programmes combined
Assuming the scholarship is automatic on admission and never submitting the emailed application form
Applying to the Bachelor in Management - Sustainable Business programme under these rules, which exclude it
Missing the programme registration end date because you were waiting for a scholarship deadline that does not exist
Missing the online knowledge test requirement for non-EU/EFTA/OECD/Ukraine/China documents, or failing to reach 30% correct answers
Not maintaining a GPA of at least 4.60 in the first semester and losing the extension of the award
Applying to a programme taught in Polish while assuming the English-language scholarship pool applies to you
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, food and personal expenses for the full three-year programme, since no stipend or allowance is paid
Accommodation in Warsaw for the duration of the programme, since no housing allowance is published
Travel to and from Poland and any visa or residence permit costs
Admission fee of PLN 85 on the English-language undergraduate programmes, which is not covered
Tuition from year II onwards if the award is not extended: PLN 21,400 per semester in year II and PLN 23,400 in year III for the English-language Bachelor in Management
Tuition for the Sustainable Business with ESCP major, which is priced separately and is not covered by these rules
Books, equipment and other study costs
document_audit: Your final-examination certificate must show the individual subject percentages, because the ranking is computed from those figures rather than from a single aggregate score

Obtain a statement from the director of NAWA about your educational certificate, or a decision on its recognition, well in advance if your documents were issued outside the EU, EFTA, OECD, Ukraine or China; this is a precondition of admission, not of the scholarship
Prepare certified translations where required by the university's admission rules
Keep the admission fee payment confirmation to hand, because it is required to complete admission and the scholarship is not granted before admission
Installments are possible: tuition can be paid in five instalments per semester (5 x PLN 3,980 in year I) if the scholarship is not awarded, which materially changes the cash-flow burden
Retain evidence of any Olympiad or Polish Championship sports achievement if you intend to claim the separate Rector's scholarship

alerts.message: The Bachelor in Management - Sustainable Business programme (English) is excluded from these rules and has its own Sustainability Leaders Scholarship programme. Every other English-language undergraduate programme, including Bachelor in Management and the Bachelor in Management and Artificial Intelligence, falls under the rules described here.

The 2026/2027 registration window closed on 15 July 2026 and no 2027/2028 dates are published yet. Do not rely on a remembered date: check the programme page or the Admissions Portal when the next round opens.
The award pays tuition only. It will not cover living costs, accommodation, travel or the admission fee, so treat it as a large tuition discount rather than a full ride.

If your school documents were issued outside the EU, EFTA, OECD, Ukraine or China, you must pass a 20-minute online knowledge test with at least 30% correct answers and supply a NAWA statement or recognition decision before your application can progress.

Only 7 full-time scholarships exist for all English-language undergraduate programmes combined, and ranking lists are per programme, so an award depends on topping your own programme list rather than on a university-wide comparison.

submission_workflow: Register an account on the Kozminski University Admissions Portal
Select the undergraduate programme, language of instruction and study format
Upload the secondary-school leaving certificate, transcript and final-examination certificate
Complete the online knowledge test if your documents were issued outside the EU, EFTA, OECD, Ukraine or China
Submit the NAWA statement or recognition decision for your educational certificate
Await the admission decision and the programme ranking list
Open the scholarship application form received by email after admission and submit it to the Scholarship Committee
On award, sign the enrolment contract (the second 2026/2027 intake set contract signing until 4 August 2026 and document submission until 14 August 2026) and submit remaining documents
Track your GPA from the first semester to protect the 4.60 threshold needed to extend the award

NAWA DOES NOT publish a bachelor's-level scholarship for general foreign applicants. The Stefan Banach NAWA Programme funds studia II stopnia (second-cycle / master's studies) only, in Polish or English at universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education, with an optional one-year preparatory course; the 2026 call required a first-cycle degree obtained no earlier than 2024. The Poland My First Choice NAWA programme also funds master's studies only. The Polish Language Programme (POLONISTA) targets students of Polish philology and Polish studies, with partial (one- or two-semester) or full studies conducted in Polish, and only laureates and finalists of the Polish Language and Literature Olympiad held outside Poland may take a NAWA scholarship for first- or second-cycle studies in Polish studies; NAWA's other Polish-language offers are summer courses and Polish-language teacher programmes, which are short-term and non-degree. NAWA's only foreign-student scheme that names studia I stopnia (first-cycle / bachelor's) is the General Anders Programme for the Polish Diaspora, but its eligibility is restricted to holders of the Karta Polaka or of both Polish and another citizenship who completed secondary school outside Poland, with studies in Polish, i.e. it is locked to a single diaspora group rather than broadly open, and the protocol directs that such an award be skipped in favour of a broadly-open alternative. Substituted therefore with a non-excluded Polish university international undergraduate scholarship: Kozminski University 'Scholarship for the Best Students' (100% tuition), researched on the awarding body's own domain kozminski.edu.pl. All NAWA figures encountered during the check were deliberately excluded from this record.
research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: Confirmed bachelor's level directly from the awarding body's own page: the scholarship is awarded to 'the student admitted to the first semester of full-time or part-time undergraduate (Bachelor's) or long-cycle Master's programs'. The programme pages confirm the undergraduate route is a degree: the Bachelor in Management is listed as 'Undergraduate Programs (Bachelor)', 'Duration: 3 years', 'Language: EN', 'Obtained title: Bachelor Level Degree', with six semesters, and the university states that the three-year Bachelor Program in Management is equivalent to a BSc or a BComm degree. The award count is streamed by programme type and study format, with 7 of the 17 full-time scholarships reserved for English-language undergraduate programmes. The parallel coverage of long-cycle Master's programmes is noted in degree_levels and in programme_detail_official, but the record is filed as a bachelor's award because undergraduate programmes are the primary and majority route.
